name: Park inactive shard workers off steady-state wakeups
description: What: Remove the steady-state condition-variable wakeup herd in PersistentGroupedRuntime without changing the configured worker fleet or Java-compatible stage semantics. Why: risk and matching work is intentionally coordinated by shard_index 0, while nonzero shard workers are stable topology sentinels; today all workers wait on one RuntimeCondition, so every submission, R1, matching, R2, and journal broadcast wakes inactive workers and makes them contend for the mutex. Approach: add a lifecycle-only condition; keep shard-0 coordinators on the existing progress/work condition; park nonzero risk and matching workers on the lifecycle condition; notify lifecycle waiters only for start, closing/shutdown, poison, and partial-start rollback; preserve exact worker counts and IDs, failure ordering, journal-before-result, delayed R2, quiescence, poison, and join behavior. Done when: focused Debug and ReleaseSafe persistent-grouped tests pass; exact topology and lifecycle/failure tests converge; the ReleaseFast 1x1/4x2 orchestrator benchmark preserves canonical fingerprint and capacity gates with raw before/after medians recorded without causal overclaiming; zig fmt, git diff --check, and full zig build -j1 gate pass; only intentional files are committed and caches, dumps, and api-path-builders remain excluded.

name: Implement bounded graceful shutdown
description:
P1 lifecycle parity gap. Java ExchangeCore provides timed shutdown and reports timeout failure; Zig shutdown can block indefinitely on worker or callback joins. Implement recoverable bounded shutdown across ExchangeCore, ExchangeApi, ExchangeApiSharded, and ExchangeOrchestrator.

Accepted design:
- Add ShutdownState { open, closing, complete }, ShutdownOutcome { complete, deferred }, shutdownState(), and shutdownTimeout(std.Io.Timeout).
- Preserve existing shutdown() as source-compatible unbounded wrapper.
- Normalize one absolute deadline at method entry; timeout closes admission but never cancels, poisons, frees, drops a thread handle, or mutates accepted work.
- Driver owns worker_quiesced and join_complete events. Retain worker handle until quiescence; claim/join only after quiescence; competing callers wait on join_complete. Never wait while holding driver/callback/execution mutexes.
- Worker or callback self-shutdown returns deferred. Cold bounded close must use a heap-stable drainer worker rather than blocking inline. Timed-out state remains closing and can finish on a later call.
- Sharded worker_quiesced means both worker exit and persistent-grouped/backend cleanup complete; outer worker continues to own inner grouped shutdown/destroy.
- Zig 0.16 has no timed Thread.join; event wait bounds application work/finalization, while the post-quiescence OS reap tail is not mathematically deadline-bounded.

Done when deterministic Debug/ReleaseSafe tests cover running and cold blocked callbacks, self-shutdown, concurrent timeout/join, sharded routed/split paths, persistent-grouped blocked stage and poison cleanup, exact once settlement, admission rejection during closing, later successful completion, ExchangeApi/orchestrator forwarding, api-surface checks, full build gates, and safe deinit after timeout.
result: Implemented typed retryable bounded shutdown across ExchangeCore, ExchangeApi, ExchangeApiSharded, and ExchangeOrchestrator, including immediate admission fencing, callback/worker deferral, retry/deinit convergence, exact poison-tail settlement, persistent-grouped terminal R2 cleanup, and explicit Zig 0.16 untimed join/address-stability boundaries. Verified core 619/619, API 713/713, sharded 860/860, orchestrator 880/880 in Debug and ReleaseSafe; full zig build gate 11/11 with 2086/2086 tests; fmt and diff checks clean.

name: Prevent cross-backend callback reconfiguration ABBA
description: P1 callback infrastructure risk discovered during raw-observer audit. Single ExchangeCore and ExchangeApiSharded use separate thread-local active-callback markers. Concurrent single and sharded callbacks can each hold their own callback_execution_mutex and synchronously call the other backend's checked setter; both miss the foreign callback domain and take blocking acquisition, allowing ABBA deadlock. Introduce a shared callback-domain marker or equivalent nonblocking cross-family detection for ResultSink, RawResultSink, and SimpleEvents configuration without weakening same-backend quiescence. Done when deterministic single<->sharded crossed-callback tests return CallbackReconfigurationWouldBlock rather than hanging in Debug and ReleaseSafe, and existing callback replacement/shutdown suites remain green.
result: Implemented and independently audited cross-backend callback reconfiguration deadlock prevention. Added a shared nesting-safe thread-local callback execution scope in exchange_runtime, entered only by callbacks that own a single-core or sharded callback_execution_mutex. Backend-local owner TLS remains for same-instance no-relock and lifecycle semantics. Checked setters now use tryLock from any foreign backend callback context and return CallbackReconfigurationWouldBlock instead of forming an ABBA cycle. Added bounded five-second core-to-sharded and sharded-to-core regression coverage, success/failure visibility assertions, and a deterministic poison-test quiescence join. Standalone ExchangeRuntime callbacks remain unscoped because they own no backend barrier. Verification: focused TLS and two-direction ABBA tests Debug/ReleaseSafe; core 608/608, API 701/701, sharded 842/842, orchestrator 861/861 in both modes; repository zig build test and test-release-safe 1023/1023; api-surface-check, zig fmt --check, and git diff --check pass. Independent audit found no defect in this setter fix. Residual P2s are tracked separately: poisoned drain can return before terminal settlement (r3s7u6e3), and broader cross-backend synchronous callback calls can still cycle (omw26j42). No commit created.

name: Emit result sink callbacks across core submit paths
description:
What: Extend src/zig/core/exchange_core.zig so runtime ResultSink callbacks are emitted consistently for synchronous submit, batch submit, and async-drain execution paths, not only runtime queued drain.

Why: Java ExchangeCore wires a results consumer after command processing regardless of submission route. Current Zig behavior only emits sink events during runtime drain, which leaves sync and async API routes silent and can break consumer expectations during migration.

How:
1) In submitCommand, publish ResultSink event after command execution in both journaling and non-journaling branches.
2) In submitCommandBatch, publish one event per command using per-command sequence for both branches.
3) In drainAsyncPending, remove the non-journal fast-path and route through submitCommand so sink callbacks are emitted uniformly.
4) Avoid duplicate events by removing redundant manual publishing in journaling runtime drain path once submitCommandBatch publishes.
5) Add focused tests for:
   - sync + batch callbacks sequence/result correctness,
   - async-drain callbacks,
   - no duplicate events in journaling runtime drain.

Acceptance criteria:
- New tests pass and protect against duplicate/missing callbacks.
- zig build test passes.
- zig build parity-diff passes.
result:
Extended result-sink publication so ExchangeCore now emits callbacks across submit routes, aligned with Java-style results-consumer expectations.

Implemented in src/zig/core/exchange_core.zig:
- submitCommand now publishes sink events for both journaling and non-journaling execution paths.
- submitCommandBatch now publishes per-command sink events in both journaling and non-journaling paths (using sequence_from + index for non-journaling batch execution).
- drainAsyncPending now always executes through submitCommand (removed non-journal fast path), giving uniform sink publication behavior for async drains.
- Removed redundant manual publication in journaling runtime drain path to avoid duplicate events when submitCommandBatch already publishes.
- Added new API: setResultSink(runtime_mod.ResultSink) for explicit post-init sink wiring.

result: Implemented typed JournalBatchPosition across single and sharded direct, queued, and persistent-grouped paths. Native XCJ3 durability remains per-command and unchanged. Deterministic path tests enumerate cold, running, singleton, and forced-tail schedules with sequence/segmentation invariants. Verification: custom serialization 7/7 Debug + 7/7 ReleaseSafe; persistent grouped 45/45 Debug + 45/45 ReleaseSafe (104/104 total); full-root compile-only in both modes; fmt and scoped diff checks passed. name: Replay sequential default journal partitions on configured startup
description:
Problem: Java DiskSerializationProcessor replayJournalFull scans journal partitions sequentially (starting at partition 1) until missing file. Zig ExchangeCore.startupFromConfiguredPersistence currently resolves and replays only a single configured journal partition, which can miss valid continuation partitions and break parity for split journal files.

Scope:
- In src/zig/core/exchange_core.zig add a default-path replay helper that can replay journal partitions sequentially from a starting partition ID until the first missing file.
- Update startupFromConfiguredPersistence to use sequential partition replay when initial_state.journal_timestamp_ns != 0.
- Preserve existing single-file replay API behavior (replayJournalFromDefaultPath remains unchanged).
- Use explicit error handling (no panic/unreachable in production paths).

Acceptance criteria:
- startupFromConfiguredPersistence replays commands from partition N and N+1 when both files exist.
- Replay stops cleanly on first missing next partition (FileNotFound boundary).
- Existing single-partition APIs continue to work as before.
- New/updated tests cover multi-partition startup replay behavior.
- zig fmt and zig build test pass.
result:
Implemented sequential default journal partition replay and wired it into configured startup in src/zig/core/exchange_core.zig.

Changes:
- Added DefaultJournalReplayRangeError and JournalReplayCountOverflow handling.
- Added replayJournalFromDefaultPathRange(dir, snapshot_id, starting_partition_id) to replay partitioned journal files in ascending order until first missing file.
- Updated startupFromConfiguredPersistence(...) to: replay the configured starting partition via existing startupFromPersistence path, then replay tail partitions (N+1, N+2, ...) with replayJournalFromDefaultPathRange; merged replay counts with overflow-checked addition.
- Updated StartupFromConfiguredPersistenceError to include JournalReplayCountOverflow.
- Added regression test: startupFromConfiguredPersistence now replays sequential partitions and restores state for commands split across partition 0001 and 0002.
- Updated src/zig/README.md journaling foundation section to document sequential partition replay on configured startup.

description:

- If no snapshot artifact exists, return a clean startup outcome (without replay) unless throw_if_snapshot_not_found policy demands failure.

name: Wire persist-state commands to durable snapshot journal and replay
description:
Port Java persistence command semantics end to end. PERSIST_STATE_MATCHING and PERSIST_STATE_RISK must create a consistent adjacent snapshot boundary, persist every matching and risk shard through the configured serialization path, report real failures, and recover/replay journals with correct sequence and descriptor linkage. Remove shard-0-only or unconditional-success command behavior. Keep explicit legacy-format policy separate from native persistence correctness. Done when restart/replay integration tests prove orders, users, positions, fees, binary state, sequences, and all shard partitions survive; failure injection is typed; full gate passes.

Audit evidence (2026-07-23): current persist commands only update in-memory descriptors and can append a main-log entry without any snapshot file. Every named ME/RE file is actually a monolithic XCS2 KernelSnapshot; sharded capture/restore always uses kernel 0. XCS2 omits next_seq and in-flight BinaryFrameAssembler state. Direct truncate writes are not crash-atomic. The correct first slice is single-core ME0+RE0 tagged payloads coordinated under ExchangeCore.execution_mutex, journal capacity reserved before mutation, descriptor/manifest committed only after both module writes, exact matching/risk failure result codes, retry-safe deterministic fault tests, and restore of binary state plus sequence. Sharded iteration follows only after the module contract is sound.
result: PERSIST_STATE_MATCHING/RISK now form a consistent adjacent boundary, persist distinct matching/risk payloads for every shard under XCM2, report typed failures, publish manifests only after module durability, link XCJ3 descriptors/frontiers, and restore/replay orders, users, positions, fees, binary assemblers, sequence, and routed/split mode. Failure-atomic staging, concurrent barriers, OOM/corruption, collision, crash-tail, append/sync failure, and independent-topology restart coverage passes in Debug and ReleaseSafe; full repository gates remain on the root epic.

name: Repair matching/risk sharding ownership and config propagation
description:
Make sharded Zig execution equivalent to Java ownership: matching state is symbol-sharded, risk state is UID-sharded, every relevant command is observed by required stages, and exactly the owning shard mutates each responsibility. Eliminate executeRouted routing that sends same-symbol orders to UID-selected independent books; implement independent matching/risk shard counts and propagate Java performance/orders/report/L2 configuration into every shard. Cover cross-UID same-symbol matching, cross-symbol same-UID risk, reports, binary commands, reset, and persistence aggregation. Done when single-vs-sharded parity scenarios and deterministic multi-shard tests prove ownership and full gate passes.

Current progress (2026-07-23): split execution has UID-owned R1/R2, symbol-owned matching, prepare-all/commit-all margin release, completed command responses, matcher-event ownership, and global RESET clearing risk/books/binary transfers on every shard. A lifecycle-owned bounded worker, fatal tail settlement, and config propagation are implemented and under concurrency audit. Remaining blockers: routed mode still creates UID-selected independent books and mixed routed/split sequence frontiers; binary split is unsupported; independent Java matching/risk engine counts and every-shard persistence/report section aggregation remain incomplete.
result: Sharded execution now has symbol-owned matching, UID-owned risk, independent ME/RE counts, one canonical routed/split sequence, every-shard binary/admin observation with exactly-once semantic mutation, deterministic report/persistence aggregation, global reset, and propagated Java configuration. Added the missing futures duplicate-GTC release proof. Debug and ReleaseSafe ownership gates pass: 4ME/2RE 8/8, risk-heavy 1ME/4RE owner routing 3/3, mixed routed/split FIFO 3/3, plus binary broadcast/merge/stream and duplicate/reduce suites recorded on the child tickets. The repository-wide gate remains tracked at the root epic.

name: Port processor runtime and asynchronous progress semantics

name: Add ExchangeCore binary payload submission wrapper
description:
What: Add a high-level binary payload submission API in src/zig/core/exchange_core.zig that fragments payload bytes into Java-compatible 5-word BINARY_DATA_* frames and submits them through existing command paths.

Why: Binary command/query behavior exists in kernel, but ExchangeCore callers currently need to handcraft low-level frame commands. A wrapper improves migration ergonomics and reduces framing mistakes.

How:
1) Add submitBinaryPayload(command_type, transfer_id, timestamp, payload) on ExchangeCore.
2) Validate command_type supports only binary_data_command or binary_data_query.
3) Fragment payload into padded big-endian i64 words, 5 words per frame, mark final frame with symbol=-1.
4) Submit frames sequentially via submitCommand and return the final CommandResponse.
5) Add tests for:
   - multi-frame add-accounts binary command success path,
   - binary query payload returning state_hash_detailed report,
   - invalid command-type rejection,
   - empty payload rejection.

Acceptance criteria:
- New API and tests compile and pass.
- zig build test passes.
- zig build parity-diff passes.
result:
Added high-level binary payload submission support in ExchangeCore with Java-compatible frame packing.

Implemented in src/zig/core/exchange_core.zig:
- New error union: BinaryPayloadSubmitError.
- New API: submitBinaryPayload(command_type, transfer_id, timestamp, payload) -> final CommandResponse.
- Validation rules:
  - command_type must be binary_data_command or binary_data_query.
  - payload must be non-empty.
- Framing behavior:
  - payload bytes are packed into big-endian i64 words with zero-padding,
  - 5 words per command frame,
  - final frame marked with symbol=-1 (last flag), prior frames symbol=0,
  - frame commands execute through submitCommand so journaling/result-sink/lifecycle gates remain unified.
- Added helper builders:
  - makeBinaryFrameCommand
  - readBigEndianWordPadded

  - encodeAddAccountsBinaryPayload

name: Reject cross-backend blocking calls from callback contexts
description: Shared callback TLS currently protects callback-setter reconfiguration only. A broader ABBA remains: worker callback on backend A can synchronously submit/query/wait on backend B; B executes its callback before publishing sync readiness; that callback can synchronously call A, leaving both workers waiting. Same-family distinct instances are also affected because blocking-call guards only test target-local active_callback ownership. Audit every blocking API entry (sync submissions, drains/waits, reports and lifecycle operations), define a typed nonblocking/reentrant rejection for any foreign backend callback context while preserving safe nonblocking enqueue operations, and add bounded A-to-B-to-A tests for core/core, sharded/sharded and core/sharded directions in Debug and ReleaseSafe. Done when no callback-originated cross-backend blocking cycle can hang and same-instance behavior remains source-compatible.
result: Closed callback-originated cross-backend blocking cycles across core/core, sharded/sharded, and both core/sharded directions. Shared callback scope now rejects synchronous submission, lifecycle/bootstrap, query/report/order-book, response/accepted-prefix waits, drains, callback dispatch, and composite paths with CoreReentrantCall before publication. Async/callback/detached paths use no-wait driver/execution/journal/capacity/publication gates: immediately fitting work remains allowed, while contended, saturated, or multi-chunk would-wait publication fails without sequence/request/accounting mutation. Preserved CoreQueueFull for cold/intrinsically oversized non-stream work and external running binary chunking. Also fixed worker exit waiting for late fatal callback/poll settlement. Bounded A-to-B-to-A, no-mutation, ownership, fitting/oversized binary, and 25x ReleaseSafe poison stress coverage added. Independent audits clean. Verified core 636/636 Debug+ReleaseSafe, sharded 895/895 Debug+ReleaseSafe on final production code, post-added positive binary 2/2 each mode, fmt/diff clean.

name: Make poisoned drains await accepted terminal settlement
description: Observed race: sharded drainPending returns CorePoisoned as soon as lifecycle flips and the poison broadcast fires, before poisonFromWork dispatches terminal failure callbacks and finishes accepted work. Decide and document the contract, then make both backends deterministic: if drain means an accepted-prefix settlement barrier, wait until the captured target completion frontier before returning CorePoisoned; retain reentrancy/stopped safeguards and avoid hangs. Cover failed callback plus skipped callback/detached/poll suffixes, cold and running paths, repeated stress in Debug and ReleaseSafe. If fail-fast is intentional instead, expose an explicit terminal-settlement wait and repair tests/callers to use it. Done when no timing-dependent state assertions remain and full suites pass.
result: Implemented deterministic terminal drain settlement across single and sharded Zig backends. Drains now track contiguous accepted frontiers rather than aggregate completions, defer unpublished binary suffix settlement, wait callback/poll/detached owners after poison, include persistent-grouped terminal R2, preserve exact cold runtime outcomes, classify late fatal registrations consistently, and single-claim overlapping async/runtime drain counts. Added bounded running/cold poison, binary suffix, R2, callback, poll, ownership-handoff, same-target, and staggered regressions. name: Preserve custom persistence callback fanout on failure
description: What: Preserve Java ISerializationProcessor storeData fanout and first-failure semantics for custom persistence commands in both ExchangeCore and ExchangeApiSharded. Why: Java publishes matching and risk persistence commands as a pair and every ME/RE module independently invokes storeData; one rejection changes the command result but does not suppress later module callbacks. Zig currently uses try in serial loops, so ME0 rejection skips later MEs and removes the pair (skipping all RE callbacks), while RE0 rejection skips later REs. This is observable P1 behavior, not the intentional serial-versus-parallel runtime boundary. Approach: keep callbacks serialized but attempt every configured module; retain the first typed StoreError; preserve a pending pair after matching callback failure so the risk command still fans out; record matching success/failure in the pair; commit a descriptor only when both halves fully succeed; clear the pair on every risk attempt and preserve validation/error precedence. Apply the same pair-continuation rule to the single 1x1 custom processor. Done when: table-driven matching-reject and risk-reject tests prove all ME/RE callbacks occur exactly once in immediate and persistent_grouped modes, Java-compatible matching/risk result codes are returned, no descriptor commits after either half fails, a later valid pair is not poisoned by stale state, focused Debug/ReleaseSafe custom persistence suites pass, full zig build -j1 gate passes, docs no longer claim zero blockers without recording this closure, and only intentional files are committed.
result: Closed custom persistence fanout parity in single and sharded Zig paths. Store failures now preserve family-wide callback traversal and the matching-to-risk pair, matching and risk keep independent command results, and descriptors publish only when both halves succeed. Added matching/risk rejection and recovery regressions, including 2x2 immediate and persistent-grouped sharded matrices. Focused Debug and ReleaseSafe tests passed; the final serial gate passed 43/43 steps and 2309/2309 tests. Documentation records the intentional serialized callback boundary and non-fail-fast topology behavior.

name: Fix persistent batch barrier and inner-ring backpressure
description: Audit after same-group batch admission found two P1 correctness defects and one P2 metadata defect in src/zig/core/exchange_api_sharded.zig. P1: a query/drain can snapshot an older accepted prefix, then acquire execution after a newer batch is admitted; untargeted terminalQuiesce waits for that batch while the driver needs execution for journal/result handoff, causing deadlock. Add a batch/barrier fence held from atomic admission through every admitted item completion/callback/settlement; external barriers acquire it before execution, without waiting on it while holding driver.mutex. P1: SlotNotReclaimed from a full persistent ring is healthy backpressure but currently falls through singleton and poisons; quiesce/close the fully delivered prior inner range and retry, including raw long-group/capacity coverage. name: Align result sink gating with Java grouping-control semantics
description:
Implement Java ResultsHandler parity in Zig result-sink publication. In Java, GROUPING_CONTROL toggles processingEnabled and callbacks are emitted only when enabled (with grouping_control itself emitted only when mode==1 after toggle). Zig currently publishes sink events unconditionally.

Scope:
- Add explicit result-processing state machine to Zig runtime/core publication flow.
- Ensure GROUPING_CONTROL updates the state before deciding callback emission, matching Java onEvent order.
- Keep behavior deterministic and shared across sync submit, async drain, and runtime drain paths.

Acceptance criteria:
1) Result sink callbacks are suppressed while grouping mode is disabled and resume when enabled.
2) GROUPING_CONTROL mode=0 does not emit sink callback; mode=1 does emit sink callback.
3) Behavior is consistent across sync and runtime paths (state transitions are shared).
4) Add/adjust Zig tests for edge cases and deterministic convergence of callback counts/order.
5) zig fmt, zig build test, and zig build parity-diff pass.
result: Implemented Java ResultsHandler-style callback gating for Zig result sinks. Added runtime-scoped processing state in src/zig/core/exchange_runtime.zig and a shouldPublishResultForCommand state machine so GROUPING_CONTROL toggles callback emission before dispatch (mode 0 suppresses, mode 1 re-enables and emits). Updated src/zig/core/exchange_core.zig publishCommandResult to route through the same runtime state machine so sync submit, async drain, and runtime drain share behavior. Added tests exchange runtime result sink follows grouping-control processing semantics and exchange core result sink follows grouping-control processing across sync/runtime paths. Updated src/zig/README.md with the parity note. Verification: zig fmt src/zig/core/exchange_runtime.zig src/zig/core/exchange_core.zig, zig build test, and zig build parity-diff all passed.
